poc_details: Duration: 2 weeks (14 days) with a 48h continuous soak at target throughput
Load profile: ramp to 120 req/s over 2 hours, hold for 48h, spike windows simulating end-of-day batch (2x sustained for 15m)
Metrics captured: latency histograms (P50/P90/P95/P99), token throughput, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, tail-latency causes, error rates
Node configs to test: 4xA100 (baseline), 8xA100 (recommended), 16xA100 (scale scenario) — include quantized model variants for each
Quality checks: classification accuracy on labeled triage set (5k examples), summarization quality metrics and human spot checks
Failure modes: planned network interruptions, cache eviction stress, model reloads, autoscale-triggered cold starts
Deliverables: raw telemetry CSVs, dashboard snapshots, cost-per-token and cost-per-req modeling, recommended reserved capacity plan
sla_negotiation_notes: Customer asks: 99.9% monthly uptime, P99 latency guarantees for primary routes, defined maintenance windows with advance notice
AE stance: align on measurable SLOs in contract, propose tiered penalties rather than flat credits; propose 4-hour RTO for Dedicated node failures
Legal ask: explicit data residency clause for EU-sourced policies; Redwood to confirm region pinning in Private or Dedicated setup
Ops ask: allow automatic fallback to hosted for non-PHI traffic when Dedicated pool degraded; restrict PHI to Private/VPC
capacity_planning_notes: Baseline calc: target 120 req/s x 512 avg tokens => ~61M tokens/hour peak; translate to sustained GPU hours for model variant
Headroom: recommend 25% buffer for burst capacity (cloud burst or reserved spare nodes)
Sizing ask: produce cost model for 6/12/24-month reserved commitments showing unit economics vs pay-as-you-go
Preferred contract: 12m reserved with quarterly performance reviews and optional burst credits
